answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can trade. Like an atlas mapping every route, the ledger records each stake, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits, and a detected fraud forfeits the bond. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest, so identity is no longer free: it carries a cost as plain as ivory on a balance sheet. Even a nebula of fresh accounts cannot overwhelm the market, because each new identity must pay its way in.
